methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $235M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Electra.aero is a Series B transportation company founded by John Langford that has raised $235M to date. The broader transportation sector includes 7 private comparables (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems among them) and no direct public peers. The narrow peer set—filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with comparable valuation tiers—yielded insufficient data points to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Stage-progression analysis proves the only applicable valuation method here. Using total capital raised ($235M) as a base proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage progression, the implied valuation is $446M. This reflects the expected equity value expansion between institutional funding rounds absent market comps.

The triangulation supports a median valuation of $446M, with a range bounded by $380M (low) and $513M (high), derived from sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier. Key uncertainties center on the absence of comparable-stage peers in the transportation sector, which limits validation of the 1.9x multiplier's appropriateness for Electra.aero's specific profile. Additional pressure points include transportation's capital intensity and development timelines, neither of which can be weighted against peer-derived multiples. Fundamental due diligence on technology maturity, regulatory pathway, and capital efficiency will be essential to narrow this range.
